scripture: You have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom and storm; to a trumpet blast or to such a voice speaking words that those who heard it begged that no further word be spoken to them, because they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned to death.” The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.” But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to thousands upon thousands of angels in joyful assembly, to the church of the firstborn, whose names are written in heaven. You have come to God, the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect, to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

ideas.text: A lot of us hold a hidden belief: when life feels good, God is near, and when it doesn’t, something is wrong. If you miss everything else, know that when life feels lousy, God is still there.

ideas: The holidays tend to intensify friction, stress, and anxiety, which can make God feel far away.
Mount Sinai gave the rules. Centuries later, Mount Zion became a home … prime real estate where God’s people could finally settle down.
David, the underdog king, captured Zion, brought the Ark of the Covenant there, and built a home for God’s presence.

ideas.text: God never promised that having a place where he is present means everything will be perfect. Trouble still comes.

ideas: In hard times, God says “I am with you.” The invitation is to live through those times knowing he’s with us.
Our condition doesn’t cancel out our belonging to Christ.
A Jesus church says that no matter who you are, what you’ve done, or what you’re going through, you still belong to God.

ideas.text: Hebrews says, “You have come to Mount Zion.” Verses like
remind us God is with us.
A simple four-word prayer ( _Whatever, Help, Thanks, Oh well_) shows that even if all we can say is “Help,” we can still come.

questions.text: What’s your version of the massage chair Darrin described, the thing you keep going back to because it makes everything feel okay?

. David captured Zion and made it a home for God’s presence. Darrin said God never promised that a place where he is present means everything will be perfect. Where have you expected a place, job, or season to finally make life easy?

Darrin named a common misconception: when we feel good, God is there, and when we don’t, we must be doing something wrong. Where have you believed that, and what do you do on days when you can’t feel God?
. Darrin calls these “But God” verses for days when we feel beat up. Which one do you need most right now?

slides.title: Life with God before everything gets fixed

parts.text: Can I experience life with God before everything in my life gets fixed?
How much of my life have I spent looking for the next thing that would finally make everything feel okay?

description: Christmas trees have been up at Costco for months, the Thanksgiving seating chart is getting political, and life still isn’t fixed. Somewhere along the way, a lot of us decided that when we feel good, God must be close ... and when we don’t, something must be wrong with us.

In Part 3 of *Up Here*, Darrin Cantrell takes us to Mount Zion, where David finally built a home for God’s presence, and finds out trouble still showed up. Darrin shows why our condition never cancels out our belonging to God.
